overview.body:
**Themis** (*themis*) ​— Divine ‌Law, Order, ‌Custom · ​A Titaness, ​the personification ​of divine ​order, law, ​and established ‌custom; a ​consort of ​Zeus and ‌mother of ​the Seasons ‌(Horae) and ​the Fates (Moirai). ‌— belongs ​to the ​Greek tradition, ​where it ​is catalogued ​under the ‌domain "Divine ​Law, Order, ‌Custom". The ​name means ‌"A Titaness, ​the personification ‌of divine ​order, law, and ‌established custom; ​a consort ​of Zeus ‌and mother ‌of the ‌Seasons (Horae) ​and the ​Fates (Moirai).".

‌**Themis** is ​divine law, ​order, custom. ‌The name ​means "A ​Titaness, the ‌personification of divine ​order, law, ‌and established ​custom; a ​consort of ​Zeus and ​mother of ‌the Seasons ‌(Horae) and ​the Fates ‌(Moirai)." and ​belongs to ​the greek ‌tradition.

PuniCodex ‌restores the ‌name as **Themis** ‌and serves ​its temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/themis/). The ​original preserves ​one prosodic ‌feature — ​stress or ​vowel length ​— rather ‌than both, ​which places ​the name ​in Tier 2. ‌The plain ​ASCII form ‌*themis* survives ​as a ‌modern convenience ​imposed by ‌the early ‌domain-name system; ​the restoration, ​not the ​fallback, is ​the form ‌the project ‌defends as ​philologically complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Greek ​as **Θέμις**. ​Etymologically it ​means ​"A Titaness, ​the personification ‌of ​divine order, ​law, ‌and established ​custom; a ‌consort ​of Zeus ‌and mother ​of ​the Seasons ​(Horae) and ​the ​Fates (Moirai).".

‌Law, right ​(from ‌τίθημι)

The ​ASCII form ‌*themis* ​survives only ‌because ​the early ‌domain-name system ​could ​not carry ‌diacritics; it ‌is ‌a technological ​compromise, not ​an ‌ancient spelling. ​The Unicode ​restoration ‌**Themis** recovers ​the full ​diacritic ‌detail of ​the ‌scholarly transliteration ​directly in ​the ​address bar. ​The original ‌preserves ‌one prosodic ​feature — ‌stress ​or vowel ​length — ‌rather ‌than both, ‌which places ‌the ​name in ‌Tier ​2.

The ​letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

‌- **t** ​→ **T** ​— ​Tau
- ‌**h** → ​**h** ​— Theta
​- **e** ‌→ ​**e** — ‌Short epsilon
​- ‌**m** → ​**m** ‌— Mu
‌- **i** ​→ ​**i** — ​Short iota
​- ‌**s** → ‌**s** — ​Sigma

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/themis/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**themis** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Themis.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"themis" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Themis".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"themis" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Themis" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Themis was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Themis ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Themis place ‌divine ​law, order, ​custom at ​the ​center of ​a living ‌mythological ​world.

### ​Origins (Myth)

‌Themis ​appears in ‌greek tradition ​as ‌divine law, ​order, custom. ​The ​name's meaning, ​"A Titaness, ​the ‌personification of ​divine order, ‌law, ​and established ‌custom; a ​consort ‌of Zeus ​and mother ‌of ​the Seasons ​(Horae) and ‌the ‌Fates (Moirai).", ‌shapes the ​narratives ​told about ‌this figure.

​### ​Worship and ‌Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ​and later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ​Themis in ‌ritual, ​text, and ​iconography, ensuring ​the ​name survived ‌into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

‌The myths ​of ​Themis survive ‌in fragments, ‌summaries, ‌and later ‌retellings. Each ​version ‌reflects the ​interests of ​its ​tellers — ‌poets, priests, ​philosophers, ​and scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does not ​privilege a ​single ‌version; it ​gathers the ‌attestations ​so that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. The ‌restoration Themis ​gives ​the figure ​a stable ​name ‌around which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Themis ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Greek ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming Θέμις, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to divine ​law ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate Themis ‌is to ‌hold the ​idea ​of divine ​Law, Order, ​Custom in ​the ‌mind and ​to ask ​what of ‌it endures. ​The ‌name means ​"A Titaness, ‌the personification ​of ​divine order, ​law, and ​established custom; ​a ‌consort of ​Zeus and ‌mother of ​the ‌Seasons (Horae) ​and the ‌Fates (Moirai)." ​— ‌and a ​name that ​carries its ‌meaning so ‌openly ‌invites meditation ​rather than ​mere recollection. ‌The ​tradition remembers ​the name ‌as divine ​Law, ​Order, Custom ‌· A ​Titaness, the ‌personification ​of divine ​order, law, ​and established ​custom; ‌a consort ‌of Zeus ​and mother ‌of ​the Seasons ​(Horae) and ‌the Fates ‌(Moirai)..

Sit ‌with ‌the restored ​form — ‌Themis — ​and ​the diacritics ​themselves become ‌the practice: ​each ​mark is ​a small ‌act of ​attention, ​a refusal ​to let ‌the plain ​ASCII ‌form *themis* ​stand in ‌for the ​whole. What ‌the ‌tradition preserved ​in this ​name, the ​restoration ​asks the ‌reader to ‌preserve in ​turn.
